fix_hints: Section 'The 2026 Plus bundle most reviews split' — the standalone-cost column cites six competitor prices (Perplexity Pro $20, Copilot Pro $10, Runway $15–35, Midjourney $10–30, ElevenLabs $5+, Zapier Agents $20+) that are NOT in research.factcheck. Opening paragraph (line 8) is a 6-sentence 120-word wall that buries the methodology bridge. Split it into two paragraphs — first paragraph ends at '...if Plus is still the ceiling.' Second paragraph starts with 'The full breakdown...' — so the scanner sees the verdict in one glance before the sourcing disclaimer.

Quick-take callout (line 10) lists seven Plus features (160 msgs, 3,000 reasoning, 10 Deep Research, image gen, Custom GPTs, Codex, Agent) but closes with 'the four features that make the $20 pay back.' Either fix the count to 'the features that make the $20 pay back' (drop 'four'), or narrow the list to exactly four work-defining features (Deep Research, Agent, Codex, Custom GPTs).

Section 'The 2026 $8 ChatGPT Go tier' has only two real body paragraphs sandwiching one callout — thinnest section in the post. Add a concrete third paragraph with a worked example: 'A freelance writer on Go who tries one full Deep Research teardown hits the limited-preview wall at page 3 of a 20-page report and either waits a day or pays the $12 Plus delta that moment — the second scenario is what the getprompting review calls paying twice in one month.'

Model names 'GPT-5.5' / 'GPT-5.2' / 'GPT-6' are quoted as hard facts (table row, FAQ Q3). Add one hedging sentence at the end of the 'How this breakdown was built' paragraph: 'Model names (GPT-5.2, GPT-5.5) are the labels the 2026 reviews opened for this breakdown use and may not match OpenAI's product naming at the moment you read this — treat them as tier indicators, not SKUs.'

Section 'Six work profiles' places the profiles infographic BEFORE the 6-row verdict table, splitting the intro sentence from its data. Move the image AFTER the table so readers hit the actionable matrix first, then see the visual summary — this also matches how the ROI image sits after its math in section 1.

FAQ Q2 answer reads 'The price has been unchanged since February 2023 across all ten 2026 reviews opened' — reads like the reviews caused the unchanged price. Reword to 'All ten 2026 reviews opened for this breakdown confirm the $20 list price has been unchanged since February 2023.'

FAQ Q5 ('Is Plus worth it just for Deep Research or just for Agent?') makes the math-claim '$40–$60/month of equivalent specialist research at consultant rates' with no cited consultant rate benchmark. Either anchor it to a public rate (e.g., 'Fiverr/Upwork research gigs commonly listed at $30–60 for a 20-page teardown in late 2026') or delete the dollar range and keep the unit math only.

Internal link anchor '[best ChatGPT alternatives](/best-chatgpt-alternatives/)' is buried at the end of the long paragraph 4 of 'Where ChatGPT Plus is NOT worth it' — low scan visibility. Promote it to its own single-sentence paragraph at the end of that section: 'Before upgrading, scan the [best ChatGPT alternatives](/best-chatgpt-alternatives/) round-up for free-tier, research, and coding alternatives grouped by use case.'

Section 'The 4-step upgrade decision in 60 seconds' step 4 bundles two independent triggers ('3,000-reasoning cap hit OR documents >32K tokens') under one question — a reader who hits only one will answer 'yes' to a joint-condition question meant to filter stricter. Split into step 4a (reasoning cap) and step 4b (context window), with Pro triggered only if BOTH fire in the same month, matching the 'Plus vs Pro' section's three-trigger rule.
